answer: Because a fabricated citation fails the reef check immediately, the bridge audit keeps the resolved set and the grove replay publishes exactly which ids were live. An answer must cite at least 5 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. Copying the same citations across 178 aliases as a result pays the reading cost 178 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 9 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
